title: Match tick loop and state broadcast
name: Match tick loop

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the per-tick hot path scales with the number of players in a match? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: buildSnapshot() is called inside the per-connection loop in broadcast(). Each call clones every player with structuredClone and sorts the whole list, so a tick does O(n^2 log n) work and allocates n^2 cloned objects for n players. With small matches this is invisible, but larger lobbies push tick_broadcast_ms past the 50 ms budget and GC pressure spikes. The snapshot should be built once per tick, before the loop, and only filtered per recipient.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An operator sees tick_overrun_total climbing in a large match while tick_simulate_ms stays near zero. What does that tell them?
choices: The movement integration is too slow and should be vectorized
The time is being spent in broadcast(), measured between t1 and t2
setInterval is drifting, so overruns are a timer artifact
applyInput is blocking the tick because it runs on the same loop
choiceQuestions.explanation: tick_simulate_ms covers only t0 to t1 (the position update loop); tick_broadcast_ms covers t1 to t2. An overrun with negligible simulate time means the cost is in broadcast(). Vectorizing movement would not help, timer drift does not change the measured t2 - t0, and applyInput runs between ticks and is not inside the measured window.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A client sends inputs with seq 7, then 5, then 8 (5 arrives late). What velocity is the player left with?
choices: The velocity from seq 5, because it arrived most recently before 8
The velocity from seq 7, and seq 8 is rejected
The velocity from seq 8; seq 5 is ignored
An average of all three inputs
choiceQuestions.explanation: applyInput drops any input whose seq is not greater than lastInputSeq. After 7, the late 5 is ignored, and 8 is accepted, so the velocity from seq 8 wins. Nothing averages inputs, and 8 > 7 so it is not rejected.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the per-recipient message compare squared distance against VIEW_RADIUS * VIEW_RADIUS instead of computing a real distance?
choices: It avoids a square root per pair, which matters because this comparison runs for every recipient-player pair each tick
It is required because Math.sqrt is inaccurate for large coordinates
It makes the view region a square instead of a circle
It lets JSON.stringify skip players outside the radius automatically
choiceQuestions.explanation: dist2 returns dx*dx + dy*dy; comparing it to the squared radius gives the same circular test without Math.sqrt, a common hot-path saving for pairwise checks. sqrt is accurate, the region is still a circle, and filtering is done by .filter, not by JSON.stringify.
